messages:
jordan: heads-up: CI for the sample app started failing after we pulled the new autogen stub layout. mypy and pyright disagree on a circular TypedDict case. showing a tiny repro below.

jordan: repro (auto-generated stubs):
```py
# models/a.py (autogen)
from typing import TypedDict
from .b import BDict

class ADict(TypedDict):
    id: str
    child: BDict

# models/b.py (autogen)
from typing import TypedDict
from .a import ADict

class BDict(TypedDict):
    id: str
    parent: ADict
```

jordan: mypy: "Cannot determine type of \"models.a.ADict\"". pyright LSP shows unresolved import on the b->a reference.

rachel: classic circular. two approaches that worked elsewhere: 1) put `from __future__ import annotations` at top of stubs so forward refs are strings; 2) turn cross-model imports into `if TYPE_CHECKING` guards and use string annotations at runtime.

ty: FYI pyright's stricter checks sometimes require pyrightconfig pythonVersion bump (3.11) or explicit string annotations. future annotations don't always quiet pyright in editor mode.

jordan: i tried adding `from __future__ import annotations` to the generated files and it fixed mypy, but the editor still shows pyright warnings.

ingrid: for generator changes: add a flag like `--emit-future-annotations` defaulting to true for py>=3.10. also emit `from typing import TYPE_CHECKING` and wrap cross imports with `if TYPE_CHECKING:`. that should avoid runtime import cycles while keeping types resolved for checkers.

rachel: note: some downstreams import model classes at runtime (e.g., `from models import ADict`) which expects actual runtime symbols; if we turn imports into TYPE_CHECKING-only, that could break runtime consumers. generator should separate runtime module exports vs type stubs. maybe generate a small runtime shim that exposes simple dataclasses or plain dict aliases so runtime imports remain valid.

ty: edge case: autogen client async context managers currently annotate `__aenter__`/`__aexit__` to return generated types. that causes runtime imports when the event loop loads the client. i'd prefer we annotate those dunder methods with `-> Any` (from typing) or stringified returns to avoid forcing imports.

jordan: agreed. for magic methods (`__iter__`, `__aenter__`, etc.) using `Any` is pragmatic. we can still have strong typing on public methods.

ingrid: can we add a small matrix test in the generator CI that runs mypy+pyright on a repo with circular models and the generated output? add options: future-annotations on/off, TYPE_CHECKING guards on/off. that'll catch regressions across checkers.

jordan: i'll prepare a PR: generate future annotations, TYPE_CHECKING guards for inter-model refs, and switch magic dunders to Any. i'll also add the CI matrix.

ci-bot: CI: sampleapp/mypy job failed -> https://ci.internal/1234/build/9999 (mypy errors) :eyes:

rachel: quick workaround for sampleapp before the generator PR lands: pin generator to previous tag or vendor the stub files into the repo and patch them with `from __future__ import annotations`.

ty: also mention this in release notes and the SDK changelog so SDK integrators know about the toggle.

jordan: will open PR in ~45m and ping @ingrid for review. thanks folks. :rocket:
